prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production seamless ground texture for PipaKlub's 2D anime park. Reference is the approved environment concept for STYLE only. Quiet low mown lawn: broad smooth soft warm yellow-green fields with only very subtle value drift, a few small irregular natural patches. Base color close to #A4B96B. This is the visual REST layer beneath characters and landmarks. Extremely low contrast, calm, readable. No repeating grass tufts, no caret ^ shapes, no scattered sharp leaf strokes, no stippling, no outlines, no tiny flowers, no leaf shadows, no visible panels, grids, border, vignette, trees or objects. Slightly hand-painted game background, but NOT watercolor bloom, not photoreal, not 3D. Opposite edges seamlessly tile. Most of the image is calm solid color masses. No grass blade carpet. Match sunny Brazilian park cel-background colors while deliberately quieter than vegetation props.

Use case: stylized-concept. Production seamless square texture for the NON-WALKABLE WOODLAND perimeter of an isometric 2D anime RPG park. It must read as a carpet of LOW CLOSED SHRUB CANOPIES, not lawn and not individual upright trees. Broad connected rounded asymmetrical foliage MASSES in muted dark blue-sage, forest olive and soft moss green, arranged in varied group sizes. Sparse interior leaf-shaped marks, not many tiny leaves; low contrast within each mass. A few large shadow pockets between bushes, but no accessible open paths. Overall value noticeably darker and cooler than a sunny short yellow-green lawn. Use flat cel-painted broad shapes, coherent navy-green contour edges between clumps, simplified matching the provided PipaKlub park style. Perfectly TOP-DOWN FLAT material texture, NO perspective, no tree trunks, no long branches, no flowers, no scattered items, no sun dapple spots, no glow, no cast shadows, no visible tile borders, no UI or text. Fully opaque canvas edge to edge, opposite edges tile seamlessly. This quiet low-detail backing frames the playable park without adding lots of tall trees. Keep saturation moderate, avoid neon yellow highlights.
